findings.what: The stage declares a behavior change that this hop does not make. The notes say that before 7.2.3 the development and test environments 'used a key generated once and kept in tmp/local_secret.txt', and that after this stage sessions there 'no longer survive a restart' when no key is configured. We measured the 'before' side, which the notes say was not measured: on Rails 7.1.6 (the S2 branch) in test and in development the secret key already equals the value config/initializers/secret_key.rb puts in the credentials, and no tmp/local_secret.txt is written. The installed 7.1.6 source agrees (railties-7.1.6 lib/rails/application.rb:478 reads ENV, then credentials, and only then generates a local secret). The stage's new example passes unchanged on 7.1.6. So the key handling is identical before and after this hop in all three environments, and the client is being asked to accept a change that does not exist, sourced to a changelog entry that describes 7.2.2 to 7.2.3, not 7.1.6 to 7.2.4. No application code is wrong. The error started upstream of the author: the roadmap review added the item to the plan and our first review of this stage sent it back as a defect, both from the changelog alone. The author did what was asked and flagged that the 7.1.6 side was unmeasured. What has to change is text: remove the declaration (or restate it as 'checked, no change on this hop, measured on both versions'), correct the spec comment, and correct the plan item.

findings.what: Carried from the first review, still open: json is not pinned below 3. Active Support 7.2 and 8.0 pass an option that json 3 removed, and the plan put the pin in S2. The lock holds json 2.7.1, to_json works on 7.2.4 (probe), and the conservative relock did not move it. Belongs to S2's follow-up or to S4 before its relock. The notes list it as a follow-up.

The first review's defects 1 and 2 are fixed and we confirmed both independently. The migration waiter boots on 7.2.4 with the schema loaded, exits 1 as designed when migrations are pending, and the new spec fails without the fix. The lock differs from S2 only in the framework gems, connection_pool, minitest and useragent; psych and stringio are back at their locked versions and the loaded psych is 5.4.0.

Two planned items remain open and the notes say so: bin/rails app:update was not run, and the client has the two column names for stored Astana values (users.time_zone, organizations.time_zone) but no query. Small inconsistency in the text: the notes say 12 framework gems move, the lock table in the pull request text says 13. Both are right (12 components plus the rails gem itself); one sentence would say so.

Carried from the first review and re-read: errors.each is called with a two-argument block, a form Active Model stopped supporting in 7.0. Not caused by this stage, same before and after. We read it and did not run it. Worth a ticket outside the upgrade.

method.changelogs_not_read: actioncable, actionmailbox, actiontext, activejob and activestorage for 7.2 (53 entries) were not read: config/application.rb requires six railties and none of these five is among them (inventory.json, framework_config). Entry counts exclude the 'No changes' placeholders. Entries that apply: the soft deprecation of ActiveRecord::Base.connection (lib/tasks/postal.rake:31, still works, prints nothing); the Astana zone; the 7.2.3 secret_key_base entry (see finding 1: it describes a change this hop does not make); show_exceptions true/false removed; the Rack 3.2 :unprocessable_entity conversion (two render calls, converted by Rails, no warning); the HAML capture fix (content_for :sidebar, always non-blank, recorded responses identical). We also searched repo/ for the removed or renamed names in the seven changelogs (about 50 names and call forms, among them clear_active_connections!, check_pending!, fixture_path, Rails.application.secrets, to_default_s, ActiveSupport::Deprecation.warn, serialize with a positional coder, enum with keywords) and found no use. We searched the installed source of 27 gems that hook into Rails for 22 of those names; the hits (nifty-utils auto_attribute_permit, kaminari and sprockets-rails deprecation calls, dynamic_form error_message_on) are in files the application does not load or on paths its calls do not reach.

upstream_diff.against: branch chore/rails-7-2-and-dependency-upgrades, branch upgrade-rails-8.1.4 and the project's open pull request for Rails 8.1
upstream_diff.why_not: None is a break this stage needed. The explicit YAML coder on the two serialized columns is only required under the 7.1 defaults; under load_defaults 7.0 both columns resolve to the YAML coder on 7.2.4 and round trip (probe). Their replacement of dynamic_form is a choice: the gem's helpers are present on 7.2.4 and the recorded invalid-form responses are identical apart from the declared time zone lines. The framework defaults files are the config stage's work. db/schema.rb and the annotate rake files belong to the 8.1 hop and to S2. The two files both sides change (lib/migration_waiter.rb, config/environments/test.rb) now carry the same change as theirs. Their Gemfile pins json below 3, which this branch still does not (finding 2). None of their three lines of work mentions or changes the secret key handling.
